VERDICT: DISAGREE. Six findings, each reproduced.

F1 (BLOCKING, measured). The commit-identity gate fails on this PR. `python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base origin/main --head HEAD` prints: 'FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot: LEAPWare <300127941+LEAPWare-HQ@users.noreply.github.com>' and exits 1. Same result with --base at the merge-base (bfe8507), so this is not an artifact of the branch being behind main. The three content commits (54eb044, 3f6a2b5, 4793afc) were authored through the GitHub contents API, which stamps the noreply address; that is neither ALLOWED_HUMAN nor a [bot] address. This PR exists to fix gate defects and fails a gate itself.

F2 (BLOCKING, measured). scripts/lwb_lanes.py was reconstructed wholesale, not edited, destroying 187 lines of the repository's own rationale. Measured at the merge-base (bfe8507) vs this head: the file goes 845 -> 658 lines (-187); '#'-comment lines go 178 -> 102 (-76); lines containing an em dash go 9 -> 2, i.e. prose was re-typed with '--' substituted. Multi-paragraph docstrings on resolve_head_sha, _is_record_only_commit, resolve_reviewable_head, _validate_against_schema and _parse_identity are collapsed to one-liners. Each deleted block records WHY a check exists and which adversarial finding produced it -- in this repository that rationale is the audit trail, and the whole functional delta it was traded for is one new frozenset plus its use in _id_segments.

F3 (BLOCKING, reproduced by mutation probe). The record-only exemption added to scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py is repo-wide, so it lets an ARBITRARY, non-LEAPWare identity author the very files that are the merge gate's evidence. _is_record_only_commit tests only that every path starts with 'reviews/' or 'proof/' -- any PR's review directory, reviews/schema.json, reviews/README.md, proof/exempt.json included. PROBE, run in a throwaway local commit and then reset (nothing pushed): I committed a single new file reviews/40/PROBE-delete-me.json authored 'Attacker <attacker@example.invalid>' with an 'LWB-Agent: claude' trailer. This branch's gate: 'lwb-commit-identity check passed', exit 0. origin/main's copy of the same script, run from the same worktree over the same commit: 'FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot: Attacker <attacker@example.invalid>', exit 1. So the change converts a hard identity gate into a pass for exactly the class of file that decides whether a PR may merge. The PR body says the exemption covers 'pure bookkeeping commits' and that directive 10 is untouched; the probe shows the exemption is not scoped to bookkeeping of the PR's own record, and that an outside identity can write gate evidence. (PR #45 narrows this to reviews/<pr_number>/ and proof/<pr_number>.json; I review that separately.)

F4 (BLOCKING, measured). No proof record. `ls proof/` on this branch: no 40.json, and proof/exempt.json does not name 40. Per CLAUDE.md every deliverable needs a Proof of Completion, and lwb-proof-coverage is a required check.

F5 (BLOCKING, measured). Both behavior changes ship untested. `grep -rn 'IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS' tests/` returns nothing -- no test covers the product-name stoplist, its case-insensitivity, or the false positive it exists to fix. No test covers the new record-only skip in lwb_check_commit_identity._authors; the only tests/ hits for 'record-only' are in tests/test_lwb_lanes.py and predate this PR. A gate change with no test is exactly the vacuous-check shape this repository has shipped before.

F6 (BLOCKING, structural -- this PR cannot go green as it stands). reviews/40/ carries six DISAGREE records. scripts/lwb_lanes._review_ok checks verdict BEFORE staleness and appends a hard error for any record that is not AGREE, and check_lanes fails on any error, so a DISAGREE record can never be cleared by adding an AGREE record -- including this one. Measured: `python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 40` prints six 'verdict is DISAGREE, want AGREE' FAILs plus '0 independent review(s)' for each of the seven claude-authored commits. My AGREE would not have changed that either; I state it so this record is not mistaken for something that could unblock the PR. Clearing it requires deleting other reviewers' records (evidence destruction, which reviews/README.md forbids) or re-cutting the branch -- which #45 does.

F7 (non-blocking correction to the PR body). The body states 'Since this is LWB-Agent: human, lwb-lanes skips shared-path review per its own existing rule.' That is false at the current head: the branch now carries seven LWB-Agent: claude commits touching reviews/40/, which classify_path treats as a shared path, so lwb-lanes demands an independent review for each of them. It was true only of the three original content commits.

NEAR-MISS I CAUGHT AND AM PRINTING, per the honesty rule. My first diff was `git diff --stat origin/main..HEAD`, which showed this PR deleting docs/requirements/decisions.md, docs/requirements/build-plan.md, docs/maintainers/session-handoff-2026-09-19.md, proof/39.json and seven reviews/ records -- 1321 deletions. I was one step from filing that as a catastrophic finding. It is not real: the merge-base is bfe8507 and the branch is simply one commit behind main (e5f29bf), so those files appear deleted only because the branch predates them. The true branch diff (merge-base..HEAD) is 8 files, 138 insertions, 228 deletions. Second near-miss: `git log --format='%(trailers:key=LWB-Agent,valueonly)'` reported an EMPTY trailer for 4af2b3e8 and f170d4ec, which I nearly filed as missing-trailer violations. Reading the raw messages shows both do carry 'LWB-Agent: claude'; git's trailer parser missed it because a blank line separates it from the Co-Authored-By block. Neither commit is at fault.

WHAT I VERIFIED THAT IS FINE. Full suite at this head: `python -m pytest tests/ -q` -> 522 passed, 1 warning, 24.39s (the warning is a pre-existing invalid escape sequence in tests/test_lwb_check_proof_reexecute.py:248, not this PR's). _id_segments IS case-insensitive at this head (`seg.lower() not in IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS`) -- I specifically checked this because #45's body says the stoplist lost case-insensitivity, and at THIS head it has not; I am not carrying that claim forward. The stoplist itself is a reasonable fix for the PR #38 false positive, and the asymmetry F3's change was aimed at (lanes had the record-only exemption, the identity check did not) is real. The defect is the scope of the remedy, not its motivation.

WHAT I DID NOT CHECK, explicitly. I did not run CI on GitHub or read its logs; every measurement above is local. I did not run lwb_check_proof.py, lwb_check_state_claims.py, lwb_handoff.py --check, lwb_build.py, the plugin validators, lwb_check_env_leak.py, lwb_check_foreign_repo.py, lwb_check_hosted_runners.py or lwb_check_hook_launch.py on this branch -- F1, F4 and F6 each block independently, so further gate output would not change the verdict. I did not mutation-probe the IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS stoplist for over-filtering (an id whose genuine session token happens to be the literal string 'buildcraft', 'leapware' or 'lwb' would now be dropped from the collision set; I did not test whether that is reachable in practice). I did not verify the GitHub account behind 300127941 or that the owner directed these commits, as the body claims -- I cannot check that from here and took it on trust, though it does not change F1, which is about the gate's behavior, not the owner's intent.
